newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firms, overnight rates jump.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firms, overnight rates jump.

text.p: Indonesia's rupiah strengthened against the dollar in slow late trading on Tuesday following a sudden tightening in the money market, dealers said.

They said trading in the spot market was quiet but investors focused was on the tightening in late money market activity, with overnight rates rocketing to 32 percent before settling later at around 25.0 percent.
One Japanese bank dealer said the tightening could be due to the weekly tax payments although they were anticipated to be lower compared to last Friday.
He said the surprise jump might also due to some bidding from state banks which increased operators' nervousness.
The money market was calm in the morning, with overnight rates declining to 11.0 percent from 14.5 percent, on the back of sufficient liquidity in the market.
Dealers said many operators were waiting for rates to ease further in the afternoon as happened recently, but apparently the reverse happened.
However, the tightening helped the rupiah to stabilise further against the dollar. Spot rupiah was at 2,428.0/28.75 against 2,427.5/28.5 at the opening.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,427.50/28.25 and 2,427.75/28.00, respectively. Trading remained slow, with rates trapped in a very narrow range.
The rupiah has been traded between 2,427 and 2,429 since last week, making small adjustments to factor in average daily swap prices of about 0.3 points, dealers said.
One local bank dealer said this may suggest that capital inflows continued which capped the dollar from any rise and made the dollar top heavy at the 2,430 level.
Dealers said inflows were also seen in the stock market, with the index staying above the 700-point barrier on Tuesday.
Short-term swaps were less affected by the volatile money market. Overnight swap was at 0.35/0.40. Tom/next edged up only to 0.38/0.48 and spot/next to 0.36/0.40 points.
One-month swaps were at 13.25/14.00, two at 26.25/26.75, three at 39.5/41.0 and six at 80.0/82.0 points.
Dealers said fears of a swap squeeze like in Thailand continued to linger over the forward market, forcing foreigners to maintain long forward positions.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,422/2,614 and its conversion band at 2,422/2,470 on Tuesday.
